rounds_per_day.max: 36 holes (2 rounds) per day, only if group is under 50 and conditions allow
rounds_per_day.arrival_day: Never schedule 18 if flight lands after 10am. Suggest par-3, range, or putting contest instead.
rounds_per_day.departure_day: Never schedule 18 if flight leaves before 4pm. Early morning round OK if late flight.
rounds_per_day.rest_day: Recommend half-day or rest day for trips 4+ nights

tee_time_spacing.groups_4_to_8: Book consecutive tee times 8-10 min apart
tee_time_spacing.groups_8_to_16: Request shotgun start or block tee times
tee_time_spacing.buffer: Always build in 30 min before tee time for range warm-up

travel_days.day_1: Travel + settle in. Casual 9-hole, putting contest, or par-3. Welcome dinner.
travel_days.last_day: Checkout + travel. No golf unless early morning round and late flight.
travel_days.airport_buffer: At least 3 hours between last putt and airport departure

housing_rules.large_groups: Groups of 8+: consider two adjacent houses over one mansion (bathroom ratio matters)
housing_rules.airbnb_vs_resort: Airbnb/VRBO is cheaper for 8+ people, every time. Resort is worth it for 4-6 or premium trips.
housing_rules.kitchen_savings: House with kitchen saves $15-20/person/day on breakfasts and casual meals

2_to_4.best_for: Bucket list trips, premium experiences, father-son, couples
2_to_4.logistics: Easy — one tee time, one dinner reservation

4_to_8.best_for: Most golf trips. Sweet spot for logistics and fun.
destinations: Any destination works well at this size
4_to_8.logistics: Manageable — 1-2 tee times, most restaurants handle this

8_to_12.best_for: The classic boys trip. Big enough for competition, small enough to manage.
8_to_12.lodging: Large Airbnb house or 2 adjacent units
8_to_12.logistics: Need block tee times. Split into groups for some dinners. Designate a trip captain.

12_to_16.best_for: Reunion trips, bachelor parties, corporate outings
12_to_16.lodging: Two houses or condo block. Resort condos work well.
12_to_16.logistics: Shotgun starts ideal. Need bus/shuttle for transport. Multiple dinner reservations or private dining.

pricing_notes.disclaimer: All prices are estimates based on publicly available rates as of early 2026. Actual prices vary by season, day of week, and booking method. Always verify current rates directly with courses and lodging providers.
pricing_notes.flight_policy: Flight costs are NOT included in trip estimates — too volatile. Recommend users search Google Flights separately.

tipping_guide.caddie: $25-75 per bag depending on course prestige and service

destinations.avoid_reason: 115°F+ temps make afternoon rounds brutal.
destinations.why_go: Best combination of elite golf and nightlife in the country. 300+ days of sunshine, world-class courses within 30 minutes of each other, and Old Town Scottsdale is the best post-round scene in golf.

top_courses.name: TPC Scottsdale (Stadium Course)
top_courses.must_know: Home of the WM Phoenix Open. The par-3 16th is iconic — the stadium hole.

top_courses.name: TPC Scottsdale (Champions Course)
top_courses.must_know: The quieter sibling. Better desert scenery than Stadium, less crowded, significantly cheaper. Locals prefer this one.

top_courses.name: We-Ko-Pa (Saguaro Course)
top_courses.must_know: Best public course in Arizona. Stunning Sonoran desert on Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation land. No homes, no roads — pure desert golf.

top_courses.name: We-Ko-Pa (Cholla Course)
top_courses.must_know: More target golf than Saguaro — tighter, more forced carries. Bring extra balls.

top_courses.name: Troon North (Monument Course)
top_courses.must_know: Pinnacle Desert boulder on #3 is the most photographed hole in AZ. North Scottsdale adds 15 min drive.

hidden_gems.name: Papago Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Phoenix muni with stunning Papago Buttes views. Best value in the Valley.

hidden_gems.name: Lookout Mountain Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: At the Pointe Hilton — short but fun. Good warm-up round on arrival day.

lodging_options.name: We-Ko-Pa Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site at We-Ko-Pa courses. Pool, restaurant, casino nearby. 25 min from Old Town.

lodging_options.name: Scottsdale Resort at McCormick Ranch
lodging_options.note: Central location, good pool scene, walking distance to restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Old Town Scottsdale house
lodging_options.note: Old Town for walkable nightlife. North Scottsdale for quiet luxury with pools.

dining.name: Dominick's Steakhouse
dining.group_note: Large parties, reserve 2 weeks out. Rooftop bar is a scene.

dining.name: Mastro's City Hall
dining.group_note: Power dinner spot. Live music. Iconic butter cake.

dining.name: Rehab Burger Therapy
dining.group_note: Great burgers, good beer list, no reservation needed.

dining.name: Diego Pops
dining.group_note: Solid tacos, great margaritas, outdoor patio.

insider_tips: Book twilight rates after 1pm for 40-50% savings
We-Ko-Pa Saguaro is the locals' pick over TPC Stadium
Uber/Lyft is cheap — skip the rental car if staying in Old Town
Mon-Thu rates are significantly cheaper than weekends
TopGolf is a great arrival day activity before welcome dinner
Spring training adds energy but drives lodging up 30-40%

items.title: Rehab Burger + Old Town bar crawl

destinations.avoid_reason: Peak humidity, daily afternoon thunderstorms, peak tourist season drives up lodging.
destinations.why_go: Golf capital of the world by volume. 80+ courses within 30 miles, package deals that bundle rounds + lodging for less than golf alone elsewhere. Built for big groups on a budget.

top_courses.name: Caledonia Golf & Fish Club
top_courses.must_know: Crown jewel of Myrtle Beach. Live oak alley entrance is jaw-dropping. Consistently #1 public course in SC.

top_courses.name: True Blue Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Sister course to Caledonia by same designer. Wider, more dramatic, massive bunkers. Equally good, different personality.

top_courses.name: Barefoot Resort (Dye Course)
top_courses.must_know: Pete Dye being Pete Dye — forced carries, railroad ties, optical illusions. Bring extra balls.

top_courses.name: Tidewater Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best views in Myrtle — holes along Cherry Grove inlet and ICW. Back 9 is spectacular.

top_courses.name: Myrtle Beach National (King's North)
top_courses.must_know: The Gambler hole (#6) is a par-5 with island fairway. Arnold Palmer design, fun for all levels, great value.

hidden_gems.name: Thistle Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Scottish links-style 27 holes just across NC border. Criminally underrated.

hidden_gems.name: Pawleys Plantation
hidden_gems.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design in Pawleys Island. Marsh views, less crowded.

lodging_options.name: Barefoot Resort
lodging_options.note: 4 courses on-site. Condos and villas perfect for groups.

lodging_options.name: Oceanfront condo (N. Myrtle Beach)
lodging_options.note: Kitchen saves money on meals.

lodging_options.name: Myrtle Beach Golf Packagers
lodging_options.note: ALWAYS book through a packager in Myrtle — you'll save 30-40%.

dining.name: Greg Norman Australian Grille
dining.group_note: At Barefoot Landing. Large party friendly.

dining.name: Dead Dog Saloon
dining.group_note: On the Marshwalk. Fun atmosphere, cold beer.

dining.name: Sea Captain's House
dining.group_note: Oceanfront institution. She-crab soup is legendary.

insider_tips: ALWAYS book through a golf packager — 30-40% savings vs individual bookings
Pawleys Island courses (Caledonia, True Blue) are 20 min south, way less tourist chaos
Fall (Sep-Oct) is the sweet spot — value + conditions + fewer crowds
Request morning tee times — afternoon thunderstorms common May-Sep
Breakfast at the condo saves $15/person/day — adds up over 4 days with 12 guys
Litchfield Beach is quieter and classier than N. Myrtle if you want less Spring Break energy

destinations.avoid_reason: Extreme heat and humidity makes walking rounds miserable.
destinations.why_go: The cradle of American golf. Nine courses at Pinehurst Resort including #2 — the most famous course in the country. Walking only with caddies. This is a pilgrimage, not just a trip.

top_courses.name: Pinehurst No. 2
top_courses.must_know: Must stay at resort to play. Walking only with caddie ($50-100 + tip). Crowned turtle-back greens are the hardest in golf.

top_courses.name: Pinehurst No. 4
top_courses.must_know: Redesigned by Gil Hanse 2018. Some say it's better than #2. Hosted 2019 US Amateur.

top_courses.name: Pinehurst No. 8
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design — more forgiving than #2 or #4. Great for a 36-hole day complement.

top_courses.name: Tobacco Road
top_courses.must_know: Wildest course in America. Blind shots, crazy elevation, sand everywhere. Mike Strantz masterpiece. You'll either love it or hate it — but you'll never forget it.

hidden_gems.name: Pine Needles Lodge & Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Donald Ross design across from Pinehurst. Hosted US Women's Opens. Quieter, less expensive.

hidden_gems.name: Mid South Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Arnold Palmer design. Wide fairways, half the price of resort courses.

lodging_options.name: Pinehurst Resort (The Carolina Hotel)
lodging_options.note: Only way to play #2 and #4. Historic property. Worth the premium.

lodging_options.name: Pine Needles Lodge
lodging_options.note: Donald Ross course on-site. Quieter, more intimate.

lodging_options.name: Village of Pinehurst rental
lodging_options.note: Can't play resort courses unless staying at resort though.

dining.name: The Carolina Dining Room
dining.group_note: At Pinehurst Resort. Jacket suggested. Reserve well in advance.

dining.name: The Deuce
dining.group_note: At the resort. Where everyone ends up after rounds.

dining.name: Dugan's Pub
dining.group_note: Village of Pinehurst. Irish pub vibe.

non_golf_activities: Thistle Dhu putting course (free for guests)
Clay shooting at Pinehurst Gun Club
insider_tips: Stay at the resort — only way to play #2, #4, #8. Package deals are actually decent value
Play #4 before #2 — some groups like #4 better and it takes pressure off #2
Tip your caddie well ($50-75/bag min) — they'll read every putt and save you 5+ strokes
Thistle Dhu putting course is free and wildly fun. Do it the evening before your #2 round
Tobacco Road is 30 min away and worth the detour — completely different but unforgettable
Fall (Sep-Oct) is best: great weather, lower rates, peak conditions

destinations.avoid_reason: 115°F+ desert heat. Some courses close or go twilight-only.
destinations.why_go: Golf by day, Vegas by night. Only destination where non-golf friends want to come. Great desert courses within 30 minutes of the Strip.

top_courses.name: Shadow Creek
top_courses.must_know: Best-conditioned course in America. Built by Steve Wynn at $60M. Limo picks you up from hotel. Must stay at MGM property.

top_courses.name: TPC Las Vegas
top_courses.must_know: Home of the Shriners Open. Solid PGA Tour venue. 20 min from the Strip.

top_courses.name: Wolf Creek Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: 90 min from Strip in Mesquite but WORTH IT. Most visually stunning course in America. Extreme elevation changes. Unplayable for beginners, unforgettable for everyone else.

top_courses.name: Paiute Golf Resort (Wolf Course)
top_courses.must_know: Three Pete Dye courses on one property. Wolf is the best and toughest. 25 min from Strip. Great value.

top_courses.name: Cascata
top_courses.must_know: Waterfall behind the clubhouse. Rees Jones design in Boulder City. Premium experience without the Shadow Creek price.

hidden_gems.name: Coyote Springs Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design 50 min from Strip. Massive development that stalled — incredible course at a fraction of what it should cost.

hidden_gems.name: Las Vegas Paiute (Snow Mountain)
hidden_gems.must_know: Most forgiving of the 3 Paiute courses. Good for mixed skill groups.

lodging_options.name: MGM Grand / Bellagio / Aria
lodging_options.note: Stay MGM property to access Shadow Creek. Strip location for nightlife.

lodging_options.name: Caesars Palace / Paris / Flamingo
lodging_options.note: Caesars properties often cheaper. Central Strip location.

lodging_options.name: Off-Strip house
lodging_options.note: 15 min from Strip. Pool + hot tub. Good for large groups who want a home base.

dining.name: STK Steakhouse
dining.group_note: At the Cosmopolitan. DJ, scene, great steaks. Perfect golf trip dinner.

dining.name: Gordon Ramsay Steak
dining.group_note: At Paris. Upscale splurge night. Beef Wellington is the move.

dining.name: In-N-Out Burger
dining.group_note: Off the Strip. Late night tradition after a big night out.

dining.name: Herbs & Rye
dining.group_note: Off-Strip speakeasy. Best cocktails in Vegas. Half-price happy hour 5-8pm.

insider_tips: Golf in the morning, pool in the afternoon, dinner + nightlife at night — that's the rhythm
Wolf Creek is 90 min away but absolutely worth the day trip for the experience
Book Shadow Creek ONLY if you have golfers who'll appreciate it — it's wasted on casual players
Paiute Wolf Course is the best value in Vegas — Pete Dye for under $100 on weekdays
Avoid Friday/Saturday night Strip restaurants — prices spike and waits are brutal. Do your big dinner Thursday or Sunday
Get a golf shuttle service — nobody wants to drive in Vegas, and DUI risk is real

destinations.avoid_reason: 100°F+ heat with high humidity. Miserable for walking.
destinations.why_go: Best food and live music scene of any golf destination. Courses are solid, not spectacular — but the off-course experience is elite. Perfect for groups where not everyone is a hardcore golfer.

top_courses.name: Wolfdancer Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: At Hyatt Lost Pines Resort. Hill Country terrain with creeks and elevation. Best resort course near Austin.

top_courses.name: Falconhead Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: In Bee Cave, 25 min from downtown. Hill Country views, well-maintained, good value.

top_courses.name: Avery Ranch Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: North Austin. Good muni-level course at a fair price. Not spectacular but solid for a warm-up round.

top_courses.name: ColoVista Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: On Lake Bastrop, 30 min east. Dramatic canyon holes. Hidden gem that plays way above its price point.

hidden_gems.name: Crystal Falls Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: In Leander, 30 min north. Hill Country terrain with some dramatic shots. Great value.

hidden_gems.name: Vaaler Creek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: 45 min south in Blanco. Beautiful quiet Hill Country course. Perfect arrival day round.

lodging_options.name: Hotel Van Zandt (Rainey St)
lodging_options.note: Walkable to Rainey Street bars. Pool. Perfect location for nightlife.

lodging_options.name: Hyatt Regency Lost Pines
lodging_options.note: Wolfdancer course on-site. Lazy river, zip lines. More isolated but great for golf-focused groups.

lodging_options.name: East Austin / South Congress house
lodging_options.note: East Austin for trendy bars. SoCo for walkable shops/food. Pool houses available.

dining.name: Franklin Barbecue
dining.group_note: The best BBQ in the world. Line starts at 8am for 11am open. Worth it once. Pre-order for groups.

dining.name: Uchi
dining.group_note: James Beard award winner. Reserve 2+ weeks out. Best meal in Austin.

dining.name: Terry Black's BBQ
dining.group_note: No insane line like Franklin. Nearly as good. Feed 12 guys easily.

dining.name: Rainey Street bars
dining.group_note: Converted bungalows turned into bars. The move for group nights out.

dining.name: Torchy's Tacos
dining.group_note: Breakfast tacos are an Austin rite of passage. Multiple locations.

insider_tips: Austin is a food + nightlife trip that happens to have golf — lean into that
Wolfdancer at Lost Pines is the standout course. Everything else is good, not great
Pre-order Franklin BBQ online — skip the 3-hour line and pick up at your time slot
Rainey Street is better than 6th Street for a golf group (less college chaos)
Uber everywhere — parking downtown is a nightmare and DUI enforcement is aggressive
If you add a day, do a Lake Travis boat day — rent a pontoon and bring a cooler

items.title: Torchy's Tacos (breakfast tacos at 2pm, it's Austin)
Barton Springs Pool or hotel pool

destinations.avoid_reason: No bad months — San Diego is year-round. Jun-Aug is busier and slightly more expensive but still perfect weather.
destinations.why_go: Perfect weather 340 days a year, ocean-view courses, craft beer scene, incredible food, and Torrey Pines — one of the best public courses in America. Hard to have a bad time here.

top_courses.name: Torrey Pines (South Course)
top_courses.must_know: Hosted 2021 US Open and 2008 US Open (Tiger's iconic win). Ocean cliffs. Book 7 days out at 7pm PT through sandiego.gov. Sell out instantly for weekends.
top_courses.booking_lead_time: Book exactly 7 days out online — set an alarm

top_courses.name: Torrey Pines (North Course)
top_courses.must_know: Same ocean views, easier course, lower price. Recently renovated by Tom Weiskopf. Great if you can't get South tee time.

top_courses.name: Maderas Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best non-Torrey course in San Diego. Canyon routing, excellent conditions. Johnny Miller design in Poway.

top_courses.name: Coronado Municipal Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Basic muni but the views of the Coronado Bridge and downtown skyline are incredible. Fun warm-up or wind-down round.

hidden_gems.name: Steele Canyon (Ranch/Vineyard)
hidden_gems.must_know: 27 holes east of San Diego. Ranch and Vineyard nines are the best combo. Great value with mountain views.

hidden_gems.name: Barona Creek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: On Barona tribal land, 30 min east. Todd Eckenrode design. Casino on-site for after-round action.

lodging_options.name: Lodge at Torrey Pines
lodging_options.note: Luxury right at Torrey Pines. Priority tee times. Splurge option for small groups.

lodging_options.name: Gaslamp Quarter hotels
lodging_options.note: Walkable to restaurants and nightlife. Multiple options (Pendry, Hard Rock, Marriott).

lodging_options.name: Pacific Beach / Mission Beach house
lodging_options.note: Beach house vibe. Walk to bars and restaurants. Best for the golf + beach combo trip.

dining.name: Born & Raised
dining.group_note: Gaslamp. The best steak in San Diego. Old Hollywood vibe. Reserve 2 weeks out.

dining.name: Puesto
dining.group_note: Elevated Mexican. Multiple locations. Blue corn tacos are incredible.

dining.name: Hodad's
dining.group_note: Ocean Beach institution. Cash only. Best burger in SD. No-frills surf vibe.

dining.name: Stone Brewing
dining.group_note: Escondido location is stunning — gardens, great food, world-class IPA.

non_golf_activities: Beach day (La Jolla Cove, Mission Beach)
insider_tips: Torrey South tee times release 7 days out at 7pm PT — set an alarm or you'll miss it
Play Torrey North if you can't get South — same views, half the price, just easier
Pacific Beach Airbnb + morning surf + afternoon golf is the move for this trip
The craft beer scene is insane — Stone, Ballast Point, Modern Times, AleSmith all within 20 min
January-March is whale watching season — add a harbor cruise for non-golf downtime
Gaslamp is the nightlife hub but Pacific Beach has more relaxed bar scene for groups

items.title: Arrive SAN, Uber to PB Airbnb
Fish tacos at Oscars in PB
Final dinner at Ironside Fish & Oyster

destinations.nearest_airport: SAV (Savannah/Hilton Head) or HHH (Hilton Head Island)
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 45 min from SAV, 10 min from HHH
destinations.avoid_reason: Peak heat/humidity and hurricane season. Courses playable but brutal.
destinations.why_go: Lowcountry charm with 25+ courses on a 12-mile island. Harbour Town is iconic, the bike paths are everywhere, and it's a more refined, less commercial version of Myrtle Beach.

top_courses.name: Harbour Town Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: Home of the RBC Heritage (PGA Tour). The lighthouse at #18 is one of golf's most iconic finishes. Tight, tree-lined, Pete Dye gem. Must stay at Sea Pines.

top_courses.name: Atlantic Dunes (Sea Pines)
top_courses.must_know: Redesigned by Davis Love III in 2015. Ocean holes on the back 9. Best complement to Harbour Town at Sea Pines.

top_courses.name: Palmetto Dunes (Robert Trent Jones Course)
top_courses.must_know: One of 3 courses at Palmetto Dunes resort. RTJ is the best of the three. Lagoon system throughout.

top_courses.name: Palmetto Hall (Arthur Hills Course)
top_courses.must_know: Solid value option. Wide fairways, good conditions, no resort stay required.

hidden_gems.name: Old South Golf Links
hidden_gems.must_know: In Bluffton, 15 min off island. Clyde Johnston design with marsh views. Fraction of island prices.

hidden_gems.name: Oyster Reef Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Rees Jones design. Water on 10 of 18 holes. Great value alternative to the big resort courses.

lodging_options.name: Sea Pines Resort (villas)
lodging_options.note: Only way to play Harbour Town. Villas are spacious. Bike everywhere inside the gate.

lodging_options.name: Palmetto Dunes Oceanfront Resort
lodging_options.note: 3 courses on-site. Beach access. Good for groups who want variety.

lodging_options.name: Off-plantation house
lodging_options.note: Can't play Harbour Town from here. But cheaper and more space.

dining.name: Skull Creek Boathouse
dining.group_note: Sunset views over the marsh. Great raw bar. Reserve the deck for groups.

dining.name: One Hot Mama's
dining.group_note: Best ribs on the island. Casual, fun, big portions.

dining.name: Hudson's Seafood
dining.group_note: On the water at Skull Creek. Old-school Lowcountry. She-crab soup.

dining.name: Quarterdeck at Harbour Town
dining.group_note: Right at the marina. Watch boats while having post-round beers.

insider_tips: Stay at Sea Pines to play Harbour Town — it's the whole reason you go to HHH
Rent bikes inside Sea Pines — it's the best way to get around and very HHH
Play Harbour Town in the afternoon for the best light on #18 lighthouse
Fly into SAV and drive 45 min — flights to HHH are limited and expensive
Spring (Apr-May) is ideal: azaleas blooming, warm but not brutal, Heritage week energy
Bluffton (10 min away) has great restaurants and less tourist markup

items.title: Arrive SAV, drive to Sea Pines

destinations.nearest_airport: MRY (Monterey) or SJC (San Jose) or SFO
destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 10 min from MRY, 75 min from SJC, 2 hrs from SFO
destinations.avoid_reason: Rainy season. Course is open but cold, wet, and often foggy. You're paying $600+ — you want sun.
destinations.why_go: The #1 public course in America. If you play golf, you have to play Pebble Beach at least once. The coastline on holes 6-10 is the most beautiful stretch in golf.

top_courses.name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: Must stay at Pebble Beach Resorts property for guaranteed tee time. Walk-on possible but rare. Caddie recommended ($75 + tip). #7 par-3 is 106 yards of pure adrenaline.

top_courses.name: Spyglass Hill
top_courses.must_know: Harder than Pebble. Front 9 is dunes/ocean, back 9 is forest. Robert Trent Jones Sr. Many say it's the better golf course (just not the views).

top_courses.name: The Links at Spanish Bay
top_courses.must_know: Scottish links-style on the ocean. Bagpiper plays at sunset from the Inn. The most atmospheric course on the peninsula.
top_courses.designer: Robert Trent Jones Jr., Tom Watson, Sandy Tatum

top_courses.name: Pacific Grove Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: The 'poor man's Pebble Beach.' Municipal course with ocean views and deer on the fairways. Back 9 along the coast is surprisingly beautiful. Best $55 you'll spend.

hidden_gems.name: Bayonet & Black Horse (Bayonet)
hidden_gems.must_know: Former military course in Seaside. Brutally hard but great conditions and ocean views for a fraction of Pebble.

hidden_gems.name: Pasadera Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design. Semi-private but public access available. Excellent conditions.

lodging_options.name: The Lodge at Pebble Beach
lodging_options.note: Guaranteed Pebble tee time. The ultimate. 2-person rooms only.

lodging_options.name: The Inn at Spanish Bay
lodging_options.note: On-site at Spanish Bay. Sunset bagpiper. Also gets Pebble tee times.

lodging_options.name: Monterey hotels (Portola, Marriott)
lodging_options.note: 10-15 min from Pebble. Can try for public tee times. Much cheaper.

lodging_options.name: Pacific Grove cottage
lodging_options.note: Charming town. Walk to Pacific Grove muni. No guaranteed Pebble tee times.

dining.name: The Bench (Pebble Beach)
dining.group_note: At The Lodge, overlooking #18 green. The celebration meal.

dining.name: Roy's at Spanish Bay
dining.group_note: Great food, ocean views, more relaxed than The Bench.

dining.name: Fisherman's Wharf (Monterey)
dining.group_note: Classic clam chowder in a bread bowl. Tourist spot but fun.

dining.name: Montrio Bistro
dining.group_note: Downtown Monterey. Great cocktails, creative menu. Reserve for groups.

insider_tips: Stay at an on-site resort to guarantee Pebble Beach tee times — it's the only reliable way
Pair Pebble + Spyglass for consecutive days. Spanish Bay on arrival day (links, no pressure)
Play Pacific Grove muni the evening before Pebble — it's $55 with ocean views and gets you calibrated
Walk Pebble with a caddie — riding dilutes the experience. Your caddie will be incredible
Afternoon fog is common Jun-Aug (the 'June Gloom'). Morning tee times have better chance of sun
17-Mile Drive is free if you're going to a Pebble Beach resort — save the $11.25 entrance fee
This trip works best as a foursome. It's too expensive for 8+ unless everyone is committed

items.title: Arrive MRY, drive to The Inn at Spanish Bay
Monterey Bay Aquarium or wine tasting

destinations.avoid_reason: Peak heat, humidity, and hurricane season. Bugs are intense.
destinations.why_go: The Ocean Course is a top-10 course in America and hosted the 2021 PGA Championship. Five courses on one island with world-class resort amenities. Add Charleston's food scene 45 min away.

top_courses.name: The Ocean Course
top_courses.must_know: Every hole has ocean views — only course in the US where this is true. Wind is ALWAYS a factor. Site of the 1991 Ryder Cup 'War by the Shore' and 2021 PGA Championship. Caddie mandatory.

top_courses.name: Osprey Point
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design through marshes and lagoons. Most playable Kiawah course. Good warm-up before Ocean Course.

top_courses.name: Turtle Point
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design. 3 holes along the Atlantic. Recently renovated.

top_courses.name: Cougar Point
top_courses.must_know: Gary Player design along the Kiawah River. Shortest and most accessible course on the island.

hidden_gems.name: Charleston Municipal Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In Charleston proper. Basic but playable. Seth Raynor design from 1925. Great if you add a Charleston day.

hidden_gems.name: Links at Stono Ferry
hidden_gems.must_know: 20 min from Kiawah. Good value course on the Stono River marsh. Quiet and scenic.

lodging_options.name: The Sanctuary at Kiawah Island
lodging_options.note: 5-star luxury. Ocean Course access. The ultimate Kiawah experience.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah Island Golf Resort (villas)
lodging_options.note: Villas and cottages across the island. Best option for groups. Pool, beach, bikes included.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah rental home
lodging_options.note: Inside the gate. Need resort access to play Ocean Course.

dining.name: The Ocean Room
dining.group_note: At The Sanctuary. Ocean views. Black tie optional. Celebration dinner.

dining.name: Tomasso at Turtle Point
dining.group_note: Best casual upscale on island. Great pasta.

dining.name: Husk (Charleston)
dining.group_note: 45 min away in Charleston. James Beard winner. Iconic Southern cuisine.

dining.name: FIG (Charleston)
dining.group_note: Charleston's best restaurant per many. Reserve 3+ weeks out.

insider_tips: Play Ocean Course on a calm day if possible — wind can make it unplayable for high handicappers
Pair Kiawah with a Charleston day for the food — Husk, FIG, and Rodney Scott's BBQ are worth the drive
Stay in a villa, not The Sanctuary, unless it's a special occasion. Villas are more fun for groups
Osprey Point on arrival day, Ocean Course day 2 when you're warmed up and rested
Caddie on Ocean Course is worth every penny — they know the wind and the greens
Spring (Apr-May) is the sweet spot — warm, flowers blooming, before summer humidity hits

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 15 min from OTH, 3 hrs from EUG
destinations.avoid_reason: Heavy rain and wind. Not worth the premium in winter.
destinations.why_go: The greatest golf resort in America. Five world-class courses, all walking only, on the rugged Oregon coast. No houses, no roads, no distractions — just golf. Mecca for the serious golfer.

top_courses.name: Pacific Dunes
top_courses.must_know: #1 resort course in America. Tom Doak masterpiece. 11 holes with ocean views.

top_courses.name: Bandon Dunes
top_courses.must_know: The original. Ocean cliff holes on back 9 are jaw-dropping. The course that started it all.

top_courses.name: Sheep Ranch
top_courses.must_know: Newest course (2020). Every hole has ocean views. Wide open, few bunkers. Most 'links' of all five.

top_courses.name: Old Macdonald
top_courses.must_know: Tribute to golden-age architecture. Massive double greens, huge fairways. Most unique of the five.

top_courses.name: Bandon Trails
top_courses.must_know: Inland routing through coastal forest. No ocean but stunning. Feels like a different world.

hidden_gems.name: Bandon Preserve
hidden_gems.must_know: On-site par-3 with ocean views. All proceeds to charity. Perfect arrival day.

hidden_gems.name: The Punchbowl
hidden_gems.must_know: Massive putting green by Tom Doak. Free for guests. Bet on it.

lodging_options.name: Bandon Dunes Resort (Lodge/Cottages)
lodging_options.note: On-site. Walk to all courses. Lodge rooms simple but comfortable. Communal vibe.

dining.name: The Gallery
dining.group_note: Best meal on property. Pacific NW cuisine.

dining.name: McKee's Pub
dining.group_note: THE post-round hub. Good whiskey selection.

dining.name: Trails End Cookhouse
dining.group_note: Outdoor fire pits. Great for big groups.

insider_tips: Book 12+ months out for peak season (Jun-Sep)
Pacific Dunes + Bandon Dunes are the top 2 — schedule mid-trip when playing well
Forecaddies for groups — one caddie per foursome, you carry/push bags
Bring layers — 65° and sunny at 8am, 50° with rain by noon
Fly into OTH if possible — 15 min vs 3+ hrs from Eugene
NOT a nightlife trip. Golf monastery. Early rounds, pub dinner, bed by 10.

destinations.avoid_reason: Brutal Florida summer heat + daily thunderstorms.
destinations.why_go: Three world-ranked courses on reclaimed phosphate mining land. Feels like Scotland in Florida. The Bandon Dunes of the Southeast.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Red
top_courses.must_know: Coore & Crenshaw. Links-style with natural sand. Walking encouraged.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Blue
top_courses.must_know: Tom Doak. More dramatic elevation, massive bunkers. Some say best of three.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Black
top_courses.must_know: Gil Hanse. Toughest and newest. Dramatic bunkering.

hidden_gems.name: The Chain (par-3)
hidden_gems.must_know: On-site 9-hole par-3 on old mine pits. Fun, creative.

lodging_options.name: Streamsong Resort
lodging_options.note: Only option. Modern, sleek. On-site dining, spa, pool.

dining.name: Restaurant Fifty-Nine
dining.group_note: Southern-influenced. Best meal on property.

dining.name: P205 Grille
dining.group_note: Post-round pub.

dining.name: Hive Bar
dining.group_note: Craft cocktails + fire pit.

insider_tips: Play all three — that's the whole point
Red most liked, Blue most respected, Black hardest
Walking is the way. Courses designed for it.
Zero nightlife — embrace it
Fly into Tampa. 75-min drive is easy.
Winter (Dec-Feb) is peak and best weather.

destinations.avoid_reason: 120°F+ desert heat. Insanely cheap rates but dangerously hot.
destinations.why_go: 120+ courses in the Coachella Valley. Mid-century aesthetic, mountain backdrop, resort pools. PGA West Stadium Course. Great winter escape.

top_courses.name: PGA West (Stadium Course)
top_courses.must_know: Pete Dye's famous design. 'Alcatraz' par-3 #17. Co-hosts The American Express (PGA Tour).

top_courses.name: Indian Wells (Celebrity Course)
top_courses.must_know: Beautiful mountain views. More forgiving than PGA West. Good value.

top_courses.name: SilverRock Resort
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design. Municipal — great value. Previously hosted Skins Game.

top_courses.name: Escena Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus design. Great conditions for price.

hidden_gems.name: Desert Willow (Firecliff)
hidden_gems.must_know: Palm Desert muni that plays like resort course. Mountain views, excellent value.

hidden_gems.name: Classic Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Arnold Palmer. Former Bob Hope Classic home. Wide fairways.

lodging_options.name: La Quinta Resort & Club
lodging_options.note: Iconic. Multiple pools. Casitas for groups.

lodging_options.name: Arrive Hotel
lodging_options.note: Hip, mid-century vibe. Great pool scene.

lodging_options.name: Mid-century modern house
lodging_options.note: THE Palm Springs move. Pool, mountain views, retro design.

dining.name: Workshop Kitchen + Bar
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in Palm Springs.

dining.name: Lulu California Bistro
dining.group_note: Palm Canyon Drive. Huge patio, live music.

dining.name: El Jefe (Saguaro Hotel)
dining.group_note: Colorful pool hotel. Good tacos, great margaritas.

insider_tips: Summer rates are insanely cheap but 120°F — only play before 8am
Rent a mid-century house — pool standard, it's THE Palm Springs experience
PGA West Stadium is the must-play. Pair with Indian Wells Celebrity for balance.
Joshua Tree is 45 min — great half-day trip
Peak season (Jan-Mar) book lodging early

destinations.avoid_reason: Extreme humidity and heat. Bugs relentless.
destinations.why_go: Historic charm, incredible food scene, solid resort golf. Downtown is walkable and dripping with Southern character. The golf isn't Hilton Head-level but the total trip experience is elite.

top_courses.name: The Club at Savannah Harbor
top_courses.must_know: Resort course on Hutchinson Island. Water taxi to River Street. Best option near downtown.

top_courses.name: Crosswinds Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best public option. No frills but well-maintained.

top_courses.name: Savannah Quarters (Nicklaus)
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus design in Pooler. Good value. 20 min from downtown.

hidden_gems.name: Palmetto Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Oldest course in Georgia (1892). Historic and charming.

lodging_options.name: Westin Savannah Harbor
lodging_options.note: On-site course. Water taxi to River Street.

lodging_options.name: Historic district townhouse
lodging_options.note: Restored townhouses. Walk to bars/restaurants.

dining.name: The Grey
dining.group_note: Mashama Bailey's James Beard winner. Best meal in Savannah.

dining.name: Mrs. Wilkes' Dining Room
dining.group_note: Communal Southern lunch. Line at 10:30am. Cash only. Once in a lifetime.

dining.name: Husk Savannah
dining.group_note: Sean Brock's outpost. Outstanding.

dining.name: Treylor Park
dining.group_note: PB&J wings. Great cocktails. Late night.

insider_tips: Savannah is a food + drinking + history trip with golf — lean into that
Open container laws — get a to-go cup from any bar
Play golf mornings, explore downtown afternoons, big dinner nights
Tybee Island 20 min east for beach day
April during azalea season is most beautiful

destinations.avoid_reason: Hurricane season. Courses may close.
destinations.why_go: Desert-meets-ocean courses unlike anything in the US. Nicklaus and Dye designs with Sea of Cortez views. All-inclusive resorts, fishing, Cabo nightlife.

top_courses.name: Quivira Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Crown jewel. Holes cut into granite cliffs above Pacific. Must stay at Pueblo Bonito/Quivira resort.

top_courses.name: Cabo del Sol (Ocean Course)
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus: 'best piece of golf property I've ever seen.' 7 holes on Sea of Cortez.

top_courses.name: Diamante (Dunes Course)
top_courses.must_know: Davis Love III links on Pacific dunes. Walking encouraged. Bandon Dunes in Mexico.

top_courses.name: Palmilla Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Nicklaus 27-hole. More forgiving. Good value for area.

hidden_gems.name: Club Campestre San José
hidden_gems.must_know: Nicklaus design. Less crowded, cheaper than marquee courses.

lodging_options.name: Pueblo Bonito Sunset Beach
lodging_options.note: Quivira access. All-inclusive saves on food/drink.

lodging_options.name: Cabo corridor villa
lodging_options.note: Pool, ocean view, chef service available.

dining.name: Edith's
dining.group_note: Open-air, live music, great steaks/lobster. Institution.

dining.name: Manta (Cape Hotel)
dining.group_note: Enrique Olvera. World-class.

dining.name: Tacos Gardenias
dining.group_note: Best fish tacos in Cabo. Cash only.

dining.name: El Squid Roe
dining.group_note: Legendary Cabo party bar. One night mandatory.

insider_tips: All-inclusive resort saves massive money on food/drinks
Quivira is the must-play — one of the most spectacular on Earth
Passport required. Check everyone's.
Use Uber — taxis overcharge tourists
Fishing is incredible — half-day charter mandatory for non-golf time
Don't drink tap water
Nov-Dec is prime: peak weather, fewer crowds, slightly lower prices

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 10 min from BKG, 45 min from SGF
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold and most attractions/courses closed or limited.
destinations.why_go: Best bang-for-your-buck golf trip in the Midwest. Ozark mountain scenery, courses under $100, lakeside lodging, and just enough nightlife to keep it fun. Perfect for dads trips and big reunion groups.

top_courses.name: Top of the Rock (Par-3 Course)
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus par-3 course at Big Cedar Lodge. Caves, waterfalls, Table Rock Lake views. Hosted the Bass Pro Legends of Golf. Not a real round but an experience.

top_courses.name: Payne's Valley (Tiger Woods Design)
top_courses.must_know: Tiger Woods' first public course design. 19th hole is a par-3 island green. At Big Cedar Lodge. The showpiece of Branson golf.

top_courses.name: Ozarks National
top_courses.must_know: Coore & Crenshaw design at Big Cedar. Links-style in the Ozarks — ridgeline routing with 360° views. Walking encouraged.

top_courses.name: Branson Hills Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Chuck Smith design. Best value course in Branson. Ozark terrain, good conditions, won't break the bank.

hidden_gems.name: Ledgestone Country Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Semi-private but public access available. Tom Clark design. Beautiful Ozark routing.

hidden_gems.name: Holiday Hills Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Basic but fun. Short course, cheap rate, good for a casual round when the group needs a breather.

lodging_options.name: Big Cedar Lodge
lodging_options.note: Bass Pro's flagship resort. Cabins on Table Rock Lake. On-site courses. THE Branson golf resort.

lodging_options.name: Table Rock Lake cabin rental
lodging_options.note: Lakefront cabins. Fire pit, dock, grills. Perfect for big groups.

lodging_options.name: Branson strip hotels
lodging_options.note: Budget hotels along 76 Country Blvd. Nothing fancy but cheap and functional.

dining.name: Top of the Rock (Osage Restaurant)
dining.group_note: At Big Cedar. Stunning views. Best upscale meal in Branson.

dining.name: Gettin' Basted BBQ
dining.group_note: Award-winning BBQ. The pulled pork is incredible. Casual, big portions.

dining.name: Florentina's Ristorante
dining.group_note: Best Italian in Branson. Good for a nicer dinner without Big Cedar prices.

dining.name: Billy Gail's Cafe
dining.group_note: Famous for hubcap-sized pancakes. Cash only. The pre-round fuel stop.

non_golf_activities: Top of the Rock cave tour
Go-karts at Track Family Fun Parks
insider_tips: Big Cedar Lodge is the anchor — Payne's Valley + Ozarks National + Top of the Rock are all there
Book Big Cedar 3+ months out — it sells out, especially in fall
Branson Hills is the budget add-on round — $40-80 for solid Ozark golf
Table Rock Lake pontoon rental for a non-golf day — bring a cooler, bring music
Fall (Oct) has the best foliage in the Ozarks — stunning colors on every hole
Drive from SGF airport — Branson's airport has limited flights and higher fares

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 45-60 min from PNS, 60-75 min from MOB
destinations.avoid_reason: Peak heat/humidity, hurricane risk, and peak tourist season.
destinations.why_go: The Robert Trent Jones Trail's Gulf Coast stops are criminally underrated — world-class architecture at muni prices. Add white sand beaches, seafood, and incredibly affordable lodging. The best-kept secret in budget golf trips.

top_courses.name: Kiva Dunes Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Links-style on the Gulf of Mexico. Jerry Pate design. Wind is always a factor. Best course on the Alabama coast.

top_courses.name: Craft Farms (Cotton Creek)
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design. Two courses on the property — Cotton Creek is the better one. Good value, forgiving for all skill levels.

top_courses.name: Peninsula Golf & Racquet Club
top_courses.must_know: Rees Jones design on Mobile Bay. Marsh and bay views. 27 holes — play the Lakes and Marsh nines for the best combo.

top_courses.name: RTJ Trail — Magnolia Grove (Crossings)
top_courses.must_know: Part of the Robert Trent Jones Golf Trail. 45 min north in Mobile. 54 holes, Crossings is the flagship. Insane value for RTJ design quality.

hidden_gems.name: Lakewood Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: At the Lakewood resort in Point Clear. 36 holes on Mobile Bay. Charming, old-school Southern resort feel.

hidden_gems.name: TimberCreek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: In Daphne, 30 min north. Solid muni-level course with good conditions. Cheapest playable round in the area.

lodging_options.name: Gulf Shores beachfront condo
lodging_options.note: Right on the beach. Kitchen saves on meals. VRBO has tons of options.

lodging_options.name: The Lodge at Gulf State Park (Hilton)
lodging_options.note: Beach resort with pool. No golf on-site but central to everything.

lodging_options.name: Orange Beach rental house
lodging_options.note: More space than condos. Pool houses available. Good for 8+ groups.

dining.name: The Hangout
dining.group_note: On the beach. Live music, sand volleyball, communal tables. THE Gulf Shores hangout.

dining.name: Fisher's at Orange Beach Marina
dining.group_note: Fresh off the boat. Dockside dining. Best seafood in the area.

dining.name: Lulu's (Jimmy Buffett's sister)
dining.group_note: On the ICW. Fun atmosphere, big groups welcome. Cheeseburger in Paradise vibes.

dining.name: GT's on the Bay
dining.group_note: Upscale option on Wolf Bay. Good for the nice dinner night.

insider_tips: Kiva Dunes is the marquee round — play it on the calmest wind day for the best experience
RTJ Trail at Magnolia Grove is 45 min north but the value is unbeatable — 36 holes for under $100
Beachfront condos with kitchens are the move — cook breakfast, eat seafood out for dinner
Flora-Bama is the legendary bar on the FL/AL state line — one night there is mandatory
Fall (Sep-Oct) is the sweet spot: warm water, cheap lodging, no crowds, shoulder-season golf rates
Fly into Pensacola for more flight options — it's worth the extra 20 min drive

items.title: Arrive PNS, drive to Gulf Shores condo

destinations.avoid_reason: Courses closed for winter/snow. Tahoe is a ski destination Oct-Apr.
destinations.why_go: Mountain golf at 6,200+ feet elevation — your drives go 10-15% farther. Crystal-clear lake, pine forests, and casino nightlife on the Nevada side. Perfect summer escape.

top_courses.name: Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Hosts the American Century Celebrity Championship. Holes along Lake Tahoe are world-class views. George Fazio design. THE must-play at Tahoe.

top_courses.name: Old Greenwood
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design in Truckee. Mountain meadow setting. Wider fairways, good for all skill levels. 15 min from North Shore.

top_courses.name: Coyote Moon Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Carved through pine forest in Truckee. Some of the most dramatic elevation changes in golf. Brad Bell design. Hidden gem.

top_courses.name: Incline Village Championship Course
top_courses.must_know: Robert Trent Jones Sr. design on the North Shore. Lake views, tight mountain layout. Challenging but beautiful.

hidden_gems.name: Tahoe Donner Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: In Truckee. Shorter mountain course. Great conditions, deer on the fairways. Best value at Tahoe.

hidden_gems.name: The Golf Courses at Incline Village (Mountain)
hidden_gems.must_know: Executive 18-hole course. Par-58. Fun, fast, and cheap. Good arrival day activity.

lodging_options.name: Edgewood Tahoe Resort
lodging_options.note: Luxury lakefront. On-site course. The splurge option.

lodging_options.name: Harrah's / Harvey's (South Shore)
lodging_options.note: Casino hotels with everything. Pool, restaurants, gaming. Stateline NV location.

lodging_options.name: Tahoe cabin rental
lodging_options.note: Best for groups. Hot tub, mountain views, fire pit. Book on VRBO/Airbnb.

dining.name: Edgewood Restaurant
dining.group_note: At the resort. Lake views. Celebration dinner.

dining.name: Gar Woods Grill
dining.group_note: North Shore lakefront. Great deck. Famous Wet Woody cocktail.

dining.name: Moody's Bistro (Truckee)
dining.group_note: Downtown Truckee. Live jazz, great food. Best restaurant in the area.

dining.name: Base Camp Pizza
dining.group_note: South Lake Tahoe. Wood-fired pizza, craft beer. Perfect casual night.

insider_tips: Your ball flies 10-15% farther at altitude — club down and enjoy the bombs
Edgewood is the bucket list round — book 30+ days out for peak summer
Stay on South Shore for casino nightlife, North Shore for quieter mountain vibe
Truckee (15 min from North Shore) has the best restaurant scene at Tahoe
July-August is peak — book lodging and tee times 2-3 months out
Mountain weather changes fast — bring layers even in July. Morning rounds can be 50°F

items.title: Arrive RNO, drive to Tahoe cabin

destinations.avoid_reason: 110°F+ desert heat. Courses offer dirt-cheap summer rates but it's brutal.
destinations.why_go: Desert golf at half the price of Vegas or Scottsdale. Wolf Creek alone is worth the trip — one of the most visually spectacular courses on Earth. Add 5-6 other solid courses, casino hotels under $100/night, and you have an incredible budget trip.

top_courses.name: Wolf Creek Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Most visually dramatic course in America. 200ft elevation drops from tee to fairway. Canyon walls, desert colors. Bring extra balls and a camera.

top_courses.name: CasaBlanca Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: At the CasaBlanca resort. Good desert course, well-maintained. Best value for staying + playing in Mesquite.

top_courses.name: Conestoga Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Gary Panks design with red rock canyon views. Good mix of challenge and playability.

top_courses.name: Falcon Ridge Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Budget-friendly option. Solid layout through desert terrain. Good for the budget round.

hidden_gems.name: Coyote Springs Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: 30 min south toward Vegas. Nicklaus design. Massive development that never materialized — world-class course at a fraction of what it should cost.

hidden_gems.name: Sand Hollow Resort (Utah)
hidden_gems.must_know: 45 min north in St. George, UT. Red rock desert golf. Championship course is stunning.

lodging_options.name: CasaBlanca Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site course, casino, pool, restaurants. Best all-in-one option.

lodging_options.name: Eureka Casino Resort
lodging_options.note: Budget casino hotel. Clean rooms, good buffet. No-frills base camp.

lodging_options.name: Mesquite rental house
lodging_options.note: Golf community houses with mountain views. Good for big groups.

dining.name: Katherine's Steakhouse (CasaBlanca)
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in Mesquite. At the resort. Good steaks, reasonable prices.

dining.name: Peggy Sue's Diner
dining.group_note: On I-15 in Yermo. Classic roadside diner. Fun pit stop on the drive from Vegas.

dining.name: Skydome Lounge (CasaBlanca)
dining.group_note: Sports bar with pool tables. Where the group ends up every night.

dining.name: George's Corner
dining.group_note: In St. George if you venture to Sand Hollow. Great burgers and shakes.

non_golf_activities: Valley of Fire State Park (30 min)
Zion National Park day trip (90 min)
insider_tips: Wolf Creek is the ENTIRE reason to come here — plan everything around it
Stay at CasaBlanca for convenience — course + casino + hotel + restaurants in one spot
Drive from Las Vegas is scenic (I-15 through Valley of Fire area). Not a bad drive at all.
Play Wolf Creek morning, CasaBlanca afternoon for the perfect contrast day
If you extend to 4 days, do a Zion National Park day trip — it's 90 min and life-changing
Mesquite in November is perfect: 70°F days, low rates, uncrowded courses

items.title: Arrive LAS, drive to Mesquite (80 min)
Drive to LAS, depart (stop at Valley of Fire optional)

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 60 min from MSN, 2.5 hrs from MKE
destinations.avoid_reason: Courses closed for winter. Wisconsin winters are brutal.
destinations.why_go: Sand Valley is the Bandon Dunes of the Midwest — world-ranked courses, walking only, no pretension. Built on ancient sand deposits that create links-like terrain in central Wisconsin. The golf cognoscenti know about this place.

top_courses.name: Sand Valley
top_courses.must_know: Coore & Crenshaw design on sand dunes in the Wisconsin Northwoods. Wide fairways, strategic bunkering, walking only. The original course that put this place on the map.

top_courses.name: Mammoth Dunes
top_courses.must_know: David McLay Kidd design. Widest fairways in golf — some 80+ yards. Incredibly fun and forgiving while still strategic. Many prefer it to Sand Valley.

top_courses.name: The Lido
top_courses.must_know: Painstaking recreation of the legendary 1917 C.B. Macdonald course that was destroyed in WWII. Opened 2023. One of the most anticipated courses in decades.

top_courses.name: Sedge Valley (par-3)
top_courses.must_know: On-site par-3 course. Fun, fast, and a great way to settle bets on the last day.

hidden_gems.name: Lawsonia Links
hidden_gems.must_know: 30 min south in Green Lake. Langford & Moreau design from 1930. Top 100 value course in America. Essential add-on.

hidden_gems.name: Wild Rock Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: At the Wilderness Resort in the Dells. Good family-friendly option with waterpark on-site.

lodging_options.name: Sand Valley Resort (cottages/lodge)
lodging_options.note: On-site. Cottages for groups, lodge rooms for smaller parties. Fire pits, communal dining. The only option for the full experience.

lodging_options.name: Wisconsin Dells hotels
lodging_options.note: Waterpark hotels galore. Budget option, 30 min from Sand Valley. More for families.

dining.name: Craig's Porch
dining.group_note: At Sand Valley Resort. Great food, overlooking the course. The gathering spot.

dining.name: Mammoth Bar
dining.group_note: Post-round beers, casual food. Fire pit outside.

dining.name: Ishnala Supper Club
dining.group_note: Wisconsin tradition. On Mirror Lake, 30 min away. Old-fashioned cocktails, prime rib. A must.

dining.name: Field's at the Wilderness
dining.group_note: In the Dells. Good steakhouse option if staying off-site.

insider_tips: Sand Valley is the Midwest's Bandon — treat it the same way. Golf monastery, not nightlife trip.
Play all three 18-hole courses if you have 3+ days. The Lido is the newest and most talked-about.
Mammoth Dunes is the most fun if you have higher handicappers — 80-yard-wide fairways are forgiving
Lawsonia Links is 30 min south and a TOP value add — $50-100 for a top-100-caliber course
Book 3+ months out for peak summer. Sand Valley has limited capacity and sells out.
Wisconsin supper clubs are a cultural experience — go to Ishnala for the old-fashioned + prime rib ritual
Fly into Madison for the best flight options. The 60-min drive through farm country is scenic.

destinations.airport_to_courses_drive: 90 min from EDI, 2 hrs from GLA
destinations.avoid_reason: Cold, wet, short daylight hours. Some courses close or have limited availability.
destinations.why_go: The Home of Golf. The Old Course is where it all started. Walking the same fairways as Bobby Jones, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods is a spiritual experience for any golfer. Plus Scotland's whisky, pubs, and countryside are world-class.

top_courses.name: The Old Course at St Andrews
top_courses.must_know: Ballot system — apply 2 days before, results at 4pm. Or book a guaranteed tee time through Old Course Experience package (£££). Walking only, caddie essential. Sunday is closed (rest day tradition). The Swilcan Bridge on #18 is the most famous photo in golf.
top_courses.booking_lead_time: Ballot 2 days prior, or book package 12+ months out

top_courses.name: The New Course (St Andrews Links)
top_courses.must_know: Don't let the name fool you — it opened in 1895. Excellent links golf without the Old Course lottery. Often available same-day.

top_courses.name: Kingsbarns Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: 15 min from St Andrews. Clifftop links with North Sea views on nearly every hole. Many say it's the best 'modern links' course in Scotland.

top_courses.name: Carnoustie Golf Links (Championship)
top_courses.must_know: 30 min from St Andrews. 'Car-nasty' is the hardest Open Championship venue. Barry Burn on #18 has decided Opens. For low handicappers.

hidden_gems.name: Crail Golfing Society (Balcomie Links)
hidden_gems.must_know: 7th oldest club in the world. Clifftop links in a tiny fishing village 10 min from St Andrews. Authentic, uncrowded, stunning.

hidden_gems.name: Elie Golf House Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Uses a periscope in the starter's hut to check the 1st fairway. Charming links course overlooking the Firth of Forth. Pure Scottish golf.

lodging_options.name: Old Course Hotel
lodging_options.note: Overlooks the Road Hole (#17). Iconic. Kohler spa. Book 6+ months out.

lodging_options.name: Rusacks St Andrews
lodging_options.note: On the 18th hole of the Old Course. Recently renovated. Rooftop bar.

lodging_options.name: St Andrews B&Bs/guesthouses
lodging_options.note: Plenty of B&Bs in town. Walking distance to everything. Book early for summer.

lodging_options.name: St Andrews flat/cottage
lodging_options.note: Town is walkable. Get something on The Scores for ocean views.

dining.name: The Jigger Inn
dining.group_note: Adjacent to the Old Course Hotel. Historic pub. THE post-round pint spot.

dining.name: Forgans
dining.group_note: On Market Street. Great cocktails, solid food. Upstairs bar is lively.

dining.name: Adamson
dining.group_note: Best restaurant in St Andrews. Reserve ahead. Worth one splurge night.

dining.name: Tailend Fish Bar
dining.group_note: Best fish & chips in town. Takeaway or sit down. Essential.

dining.name: Vic's Bar
dining.group_note: Traditional Scottish pub. Good whisky selection. Locals' favorite.

non_golf_activities: Walk along West Sands beach (Chariots of Fire)
insider_tips: Enter the Old Course ballot early — results come at 4pm, 2 days before. Have a backup plan.
If you miss the ballot, show up as a single at dawn for a walk-on — it works more than you'd think
A caddie on the Old Course is non-negotiable. They know every hidden bunker and slope.
Play Kingsbarns the day before the Old Course — it's spectacular and gets you links-ready
Bring rain gear and layers for EVERY round. Scottish weather changes every 30 minutes.
Pint at the Jigger Inn after the Old Course is a sacred ritual. Don't skip it.
Passport required. Check visa requirements. No issues for US citizens for short stays.
Rent a car — courses are spread out and public transport to Carnoustie/Kingsbarns is limited
Kingsbarns Distillery is 10 min from the golf course — combine the two for a great day
A Scotland trip works best as 4-5 days to justify the travel. Don't rush it.

items.title: Arrive EDI, drive to St Andrews (90 min)
Celebration dinner at The Seafood Restaurant

destinations.avoid_reason: Brutal humidity and afternoon thunderstorms make golf miserable. Courses get stressed too.
destinations.why_go: Historic charm meets championship golf. Cobblestone streets, world-class restaurants, and Lowcountry courses with marsh views. Charleston is the thinking man's golf trip — incredible food scene after your round.

top_courses.name: Kiawah Island Ocean Course
top_courses.must_know: Host of the 2021 PGA Championship. Walking only before noon with caddie. Book as resort package to save $100+. Wind changes everything — can vary 8 clubs day to day.
top_courses.walking_policy: Walking only before noon, caddies encouraged

top_courses.name: Kiawah Island Osprey Point
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design. Most playable of the Kiawah courses. Lagoons, marsh, and maritime forest. Great warm-up round before Ocean Course.

top_courses.name: The Links at Stono Ferry
top_courses.must_know: Best value near Charleston. Former Revolutionary War site. Marsh views without the resort price tag.

top_courses.name: Patriots Point Links
top_courses.must_know: Play next to the USS Yorktown aircraft carrier. Harbor views on every hole. Short but fun — perfect arrival day round.

top_courses.name: RiverTowne Country Club
top_courses.must_know: Arnold Palmer design on the Wando River. Former Charleston Open venue. Good test without the Kiawah price tag.

hidden_gems.name: Charleston Municipal Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Oldest muni in Charleston. No frills but great bones and $25 walking rate.

hidden_gems.name: Shadowmoss Plantation
hidden_gems.must_know: Solid conditioning, surprisingly quiet. Locals' favorite value play.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah Island Golf Resort (The Sanctuary)
lodging_options.note: Full luxury. Walking distance to Ocean Course. Pool, spa, beach. Book golf packages for best rates.

lodging_options.name: Kiawah/Seabrook Island VRBO rentals
lodging_options.note: 4-6 bedroom houses. Split among 8-12 guys for great value. Still get resort golf access.

lodging_options.name: Hotel Bennett / The Vendue
lodging_options.note: Stay downtown for the restaurant scene. 30-45 min drive to Kiawah courses.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn Mt. Pleasant
lodging_options.note: Clean, central to both downtown and Kiawah. Good budget base.

dining.name: Husk
dining.must_know: Sean Brock's legendary Southern restaurant. Reservations essential. Menu changes daily.

dining.name: The Ordinary
dining.must_know: Best oyster bar in the South. Raw bar + craft cocktails. Great for groups.

dining.name: Rodney Scott's BBQ
dining.must_know: James Beard Award-winning whole hog BBQ. No-brainer group dinner. BYOB allowed.

dining.name: Fleet Landing
dining.must_know: Waterfront seafood on the harbor. Sunset views. Book the patio for groups.

non_golf_activities: Historic downtown walking tour (2 hrs, free-$25)
Deep sea fishing charter ($200-400/person half day)
King Street shopping and bar hopping
Shem Creek waterfront bars and restaurants
insider_tips: Play Kiawah Ocean Course on day 2 — use day 1 for a warm-up round and to adjust to the humidity.
Book a Kiawah resort package even if you're staying downtown — it saves $100+ per Ocean Course round.
Shem Creek in Mt. Pleasant is the locals' spot for post-round drinks. Skip the tourist bars on Market St.
Spring (Mar-May) has the best combo of weather and availability. Fall is peak season and books fast.
If you're a group of 8+, rent a house on Seabrook Island — half the price of Kiawah with the same beach access.

activities: Afternoon round at Patriots Point Links ($65)
Dinner at Fleet Landing on the harbor
Morning tee time at Kiawah Ocean Course ($450)
Breakfast at Callie's Hot Little Biscuit

destinations.avoid_reason: Tennessee humidity is suffocating. 95°F+ with 80%+ humidity. Courses get burnt out.
destinations.why_go: Best nightlife scene for a golf trip outside Scottsdale. Broadway honky-tonks, hot chicken, and surprisingly good golf within 30 minutes. Perfect for the crew that wants 18 holes and 18 beers.

top_courses.name: Gaylord Springs Golf Links
top_courses.must_know: Best public course near Nashville. Larry Nelson design on the Cumberland River. Well-conditioned and challenging. 20 min from downtown.

top_courses.name: Hermitage Golf Course (Presidents Reserve)
top_courses.must_know: 36-hole facility. Presidents Reserve is the championship course — hosted Web.com Tour events. General's Retreat is more forgiving.

top_courses.name: Nashville Golf & Athletic Club
top_courses.must_know: Solid muni-style course. Good value for Nashville. Nothing fancy but well-maintained.

top_courses.name: The Course at Sewanee
top_courses.must_know: 90 min from Nashville but worth the drive. On the Cumberland Plateau with mountain views. Absurdly cheap for the scenery.

hidden_gems.name: McCabe Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Nashville's beloved muni. Walking only, cash vibes. Par-67 but fun.

hidden_gems.name: Greystone Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: 30 min east of Nashville in Dickson. Great shape, nobody knows about it.

lodging_options.name: Graduate Nashville / Virgin Hotels
lodging_options.note: Walking distance to Broadway. Perfect for nightlife-focused trips.

lodging_options.name: East Nashville Airbnb houses
lodging_options.note: Trendy neighborhood. 4-5 bedroom houses split well for groups. 10 min to everything.

lodging_options.name: Drury Inn & Suites
lodging_options.note: Free breakfast and evening drinks. Hard to beat for value.

dining.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
dining.must_know: The hot chicken pilgrimage. Get 'Damn Hot' if you dare. Lines are long — go off-peak.

dining.name: Martin's Bar-B-Que Joint
dining.must_know: Whole hog BBQ. Get the Redneck Taco (cornbread + pulled pork). Multiple locations.

dining.name: The Catbird Seat
dining.must_know: 17-seat chef's counter. Reservations book months out. Bucket list dining.

dining.name: Acme Feed & Seed
dining.must_know: Multi-level restaurant/bar on Broadway with rooftop. Great group spot.

non_golf_activities: Whiskey distillery tours — Nelson's Green Brier, Corsair ($15-25)
insider_tips: Play golf in the morning, Broadway at night. Nashville's nightlife doesn't peak until 10pm.
Skip the pedal taverns on Broadway — they're tourist traps. Walk between bars instead.
Gaylord Springs is the group consensus best course. Book early for weekend tee times.
East Nashville has better restaurants than Broadway. Uber over for dinner, then Broadway for drinks.
If you're 12+ guys, book a party bus for the day — it's cheaper than individual Ubers and way more fun.

activities: Morning round at Hermitage Presidents Reserve ($75)

destinations.nearest_airport: VPS (Destin-Ft Walton) or ECP (Panama City Beach)
destinations.avoid_reason: Extreme heat, humidity, and afternoon thunderstorms daily. Hurricane season too.
destinations.why_go: White sand beaches + affordable golf + Destin's restaurant scene. Perfect bachelor party or buddy trip destination where golf is the morning activity and the beach/bars are the afternoon.

top_courses.name: Sandestin Raven Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Best course in the Destin area. Robert Trent Jones Jr. design. Tight with lots of water. Inside Sandestin resort.

top_courses.name: Regatta Bay Golf & Yacht Club
top_courses.must_know: Choctawhatchee Bay views. Well-maintained. Great group-friendly layout.

top_courses.name: Camp Creek Golf Club
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design along 30A. Best conditioning in the area. Upscale but worth it.

top_courses.name: The Courses at Burnt Pine
top_courses.must_know: Rees Jones design inside Sandestin. More exclusive feel. Best greens in the Emerald Coast.

hidden_gems.name: Fort Walton Beach Golf Club (Oaks Course)
hidden_gems.must_know: Solid muni with surprising character. Oaks course is the better of the two.

hidden_gems.name: Santa Rosa Golf & Beach Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Right on 30A. Beach access after your round. Perfect combo day.

lodging_options.name: Sandestin Golf and Beach Resort
lodging_options.note: Full resort with 4 golf courses. Condos available for groups. Pools, beach, bars on-site.

lodging_options.name: Destin/30A VRBO beach houses
lodging_options.note: Beach houses with pools. Split 8-12 ways. Walking distance to restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Henderson Park Inn / Holiday Inn Destin
lodging_options.note: Beachfront without the resort price. Good for smaller groups.

dining.name: Boshamps Seafood & Oyster House
dining.must_know: Best waterfront dining in Destin Harbor. Sunset views. Book ahead.

dining.name: The Back Porch
dining.must_know: Beach-side seafood on Scenic Hwy 98. Casual, great grouper. No reservations — show up early.

dining.name: McGuire's Irish Pub
dining.must_know: Legendary steaks, own-brewed beer, dollar bills on the ceiling. Group must-do.

dining.name: The Craft Bar 30A
dining.must_know: Craft cocktails in Grayton Beach. More upscale 30A vibe.

non_golf_activities: Charter deep sea fishing ($200-350/person half day)
insider_tips: Crab Island is the real move — rent a pontoon, anchor at the sandbar, and hang out with 100 other boats. It's a floating party.
Spring (Mar-May) is the sweet spot: warm enough for beach, not yet sweltering, and courses are in peak shape.
Stay on 30A for a more upscale vibe, stay in Destin proper for nightlife and affordability.
Sandestin resort packages bundle golf + lodging and save 20-30% vs. booking separately.
Twilight rates drop dramatically after 2pm — play a quick 18 and still make happy hour.

destinations.avoid_reason: Afternoon thunderstorms daily in summer. 95°F with extreme humidity.
destinations.why_go: More top-100 public courses within 30 minutes than anywhere in Florida. Tons of lodging options, easy flights from everywhere, and enough non-golf entertainment to keep any group happy.

top_courses.name: Streamsong Red
top_courses.must_know: 90 min from Orlando but worth every minute. Coore/Crenshaw design. Walking-only feel in central Florida. One of the best public courses in America.

top_courses.name: Orange County National (Panther Lake)
top_courses.must_know: Former PGA Tour Q-School venue. 36 holes. Panther Lake is the championship layout — long, well-bunkered. Crooked Cat is more fun.

top_courses.name: Reunion Resort (Watson Course)
top_courses.must_know: Tom Watson design. Three courses at Reunion — Watson, Palmer, Nicklaus. Stay-and-play packages are the move.

top_courses.name: ChampionsGate (International)
top_courses.must_know: Greg Norman design. 36 holes — International is the tougher, links-style layout. National is more traditional Florida.

hidden_gems.name: Shingle Creek Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: David Harman design right on I-Drive. Underrated conditioning. Convenient location.

hidden_gems.name: Dubsdread Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Orlando's oldest public course. Walking-friendly muni with real character.

lodging_options.name: Reunion Resort
lodging_options.note: Condos and townhomes. On-site golf, pools, lazy river. Best group value.

lodging_options.name: Omni Orlando at ChampionsGate
lodging_options.note: Full resort with 36 holes. Pool complex, spa, restaurants.

lodging_options.name: Champions Gate/Reunion VRBO
lodging_options.note: 6-8 bedroom vacation homes with private pools. Perfect for 8-16 guys.

lodging_options.name: Wyndham/Holiday Inn I-Drive
lodging_options.note: Central to everything. Tons of restaurant options walking distance.

dining.name: Christner's Prime Steak & Lobster
dining.must_know: Old-school steakhouse. Massive portions. Classic post-round celebration dinner.

dining.name: Pig Floyd's Urban Barbakoa
dining.must_know: Asian-Latin BBQ fusion. Unique and delicious. Great for groups.

dining.name: 4Rivers Smokehouse
dining.must_know: Best BBQ in Orlando. Multiple locations. Brisket is the move.

insider_tips: Streamsong is 90 min south but is a must-play if you can fit it in. Book a 2-night stay-and-play for all 3 courses.
Reunion Resort is the best value for groups: 3 courses on-site, vacation homes with pools, and Publix nearby for groceries.
Book morning tee times in shoulder season — afternoon thunderstorms roll in like clockwork at 3pm.
Orange County National is the best bang-for-buck championship experience. Two solid courses, all day.
Stay away from the Disney area — traffic is brutal and everything costs 2x more.

activities: Morning round at Orange County National Panther Lake ($120)

destinations.avoid_reason: Virginia heat and humidity. Not unbearable but not ideal.
destinations.why_go: Colonial history meets championship golf. Kingsmill Resort hosted the PGA Tour for 40 years. Perfect for father-son trips — golf by day, Williamsburg history by evening.

top_courses.name: Kingsmill Resort (River Course)
top_courses.must_know: Former LPGA Tour venue. Pete Dye design on the James River. 17 and 18 are spectacular river holes.

top_courses.name: Golden Horseshoe (Gold Course)
top_courses.must_know: Robert Trent Jones Sr. design. Part of Colonial Williamsburg. Classic layout with ravines and elevation changes.

top_courses.name: Williamsburg National (Jamestown Course)
top_courses.must_know: Good value option. Well-conditioned and playable for all skill levels.

hidden_gems.name: Ford's Colony (Marsh Hawk)
hidden_gems.must_know: Dan Maples design. Three 9s — Marsh Hawk is the best combo. Semi-private gem.

hidden_gems.name: Kiskiack Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Built on Revolutionary War battlefield. Great value and unique history.

lodging_options.name: Kingsmill Resort
lodging_options.note: On the James River. 3 courses, spa, pools. Stay-and-play packages available.

lodging_options.name: Colonial Williamsburg Lodge
lodging_options.note: Stay in Colonial Williamsburg itself. Walk to Golden Horseshoe.

lodging_options.name: Great Wolf Lodge / Country Inn
lodging_options.note: Family-friendly options with pools and activities.

dining.name: The Fat Canary
dining.must_know: Best restaurant in Williamsburg. New American cuisine. Reservations essential.

dining.name: Pierce's Pitt Bar-B-Que
dining.must_know: Iconic Virginia BBQ since 1971. Pulled pork and coleslaw. Cash vibes.

dining.name: Alewerks Brewing
dining.must_know: Local brewery with solid food. Great post-round spot.

insider_tips: Kingsmill River Course 17 and 18 are two of the best finishing holes on the East Coast. Play the round just for those.
Colonial Williamsburg is genuinely cool, not just for history buffs. The taverns serve colonial-era food and drink.
Fall foliage (Oct) makes the courses absolutely stunning. Best time to visit.
If your group is split on activities, Busch Gardens is right there for non-golfers.

activities: Morning round at Kingsmill River Course ($150)
Morning round at Golden Horseshoe Gold ($120)

destinations.avoid_reason: Georgia heat. 95°F+ and humid.
destinations.why_go: Six championship courses on one property around Lake Oconee. Exclusive resort feel with Ritz-Carlton service. No distractions — pure golf immersion. Perfect for corporate retreats.

top_courses.name: Reynolds Great Waters
top_courses.must_know: Jack Nicklaus design. 9 holes on the lake shore. Hosted PGA Tour Champions. The flagship course.

top_courses.name: Reynolds Oconee
top_courses.must_know: Rees Jones design. More strategic than Great Waters. Excellent greens.

top_courses.name: Reynolds Creek Club
top_courses.must_know: Jim Engh design. More playable — good for mixed-handicap groups.

top_courses.name: Reynolds National
top_courses.must_know: Tom Fazio design. Private but accessible through resort stays. Tightest of the Reynolds courses.

hidden_gems.name: Cuscowilla Golf Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Coore/Crenshaw design across the lake. Walking-friendly. Different vibe than Reynolds.

hidden_gems.name: Harbor Club
hidden_gems.must_know: Tom Weiskopf design on Lake Oconee. Public access, solid value alternative.

lodging_options.name: The Ritz-Carlton Reynolds, Lake Oconee
lodging_options.note: Full luxury. Spa, lake activities, multiple restaurants. Golf packages bundle courses.

lodging_options.name: Reynolds Lake Oconee Cottages
lodging_options.note: Multi-bedroom cottages. Great for groups of 6-12. Full kitchen, porch views.

lodging_options.name: Country Inn or Holiday Inn Express (Greensboro)
lodging_options.note: Off-property but 10-15 min drive. Saves significant $$$.

dining.name: Georgia's at the Ritz-Carlton
dining.must_know: Fine dining with lake views. Jacket suggested. Group dinner here is the move.

dining.name: Linger Longer Steakhouse
dining.must_know: Thick-cut steaks and bourbon. Classic golf trip dinner.

dining.name: The Lake Club Grill
dining.must_know: Casual lakefront dining. Burgers and craft beer post-round.

non_golf_activities: Bass fishing on Lake Oconee ($250-400 guided)
insider_tips: Great Waters is the must-play, but Oconee gives it a run for best course on property.
Book a 3-course package through the resort — it saves 15-20% vs. individual green fees.
Lake Oconee is 90 min from Atlanta but feels like another world. That's the point.
Bring a fishing rod — the lake has incredible largemouth bass and you can fish between rounds.
Fall (Oct-Nov) has the best rates, best weather, and fall color on the courses.

activities: Arrive ATL, drive to Reynolds (90 min)
Breakfast at the Ritz, depart ATL

destinations.avoid_reason: Alabama summer heat is punishing. 95°F+ with oppressive humidity.
destinations.why_go: The best value in American golf, period. 11 sites, 26 courses, 468 holes of championship golf designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr. — all at public course prices. Play 3-4 sites in one trip for what you'd pay for one round at Pebble Beach.

top_courses.name: Ross Bridge
top_courses.must_know: Longest course on the Trail at 8,191 yards from the tips. Renaissance Hotel on-site. Best single stop on the Trail.

top_courses.name: Grand National (Links Course)
top_courses.must_know: In Opelika near Auburn. 54 holes across 3 courses. Links Course has spectacular lake views. Named #1 public course in the US by Golf Digest.

top_courses.name: Oxmoor Valley (Ridge Course)
top_courses.must_know: In Birmingham. Three courses — Ridge is the most dramatic with elevation changes through the valley. Short Course is a fun par-3.

top_courses.name: Capitol Hill (Judge Course)
top_courses.must_know: In Prattville near Montgomery. 54 holes. Judge Course is the flagship — hosted LPGA Tour events. Brutally long.

hidden_gems.name: Silver Lakes (Heartbreaker Course)
hidden_gems.must_know: In Anniston. Beautiful mountain setting. Heartbreaker course earns its name.

hidden_gems.name: Cambrian Ridge (Canyon Course)
hidden_gems.must_know: In Greenville. Dramatic canyon terrain. 27 holes — Canyon 9 is the star.

lodging_options.name: Renaissance Ross Bridge Golf Resort
lodging_options.note: On-site at Ross Bridge. Full resort with spa and pool. Best base for Birmingham stops.

lodging_options.name: Marriott Prattville at Capitol Hill
lodging_options.note: On-site at Capitol Hill. Walking distance to all 3 courses.

lodging_options.name: Hampton Inn (various cities)
lodging_options.note: Chain hotels at every Trail stop. Clean, cheap, reliable.

dining.name: Saw's BBQ (Birmingham)
dining.must_know: James Beard semifinalist. Get the smoked chicken with white sauce. Alabama BBQ at its finest.

dining.name: Highlands Bar & Grill (Birmingham)
dining.must_know: James Beard Award for Outstanding Restaurant. Frank Stitt's masterpiece. Reservations required.

dining.name: The Depot (Auburn)
dining.must_know: Near Grand National. Converted train station. Good steaks and local beer.

non_golf_activities: Back Forty Beer Company brewery tour ($10)
insider_tips: The Trail Pass is the best deal in golf. Multi-round packages bring costs down to $35-50/round.
Birmingham (Ross Bridge + Oxmoor Valley) is the best base. Two Trail sites within 20 minutes of each other.
Don't try to hit every Trail site in one trip. Pick 2-3 sites and play deep — most have 36-54 holes.
Grand National Links Course is the crown jewel. If you play one course on the Trail, make it this one.
Alabama's cost of living means everything is cheap — dinner for the crew at Saw's BBQ runs $12-15/person.

activities: Arrive BHM, check into Ross Bridge
Afternoon round at Oxmoor Valley Ridge ($70)
Afternoon 9 at Grand National Short Course ($25)
Morning round at Grand National Links ($70)
Afternoon round at Grand National Lake ($70)

destinations.avoid_reason: Courses closed or in rough shape. Cold, windy, miserable.
destinations.why_go: New England charm meets links-style golf. Ocean breezes, lobster rolls after your round, and some surprisingly good public courses. Perfect summer escape for northeast golfers.

top_courses.name: Highland Links
top_courses.must_know: Oldest course on Cape Cod (1892). Clifftop views of the Atlantic. Walking only. Don't expect Augusta conditions — expect Scotland.

top_courses.name: Cranberry Valley Golf Course
top_courses.must_know: Best-conditioned public course on the Cape. Tight fairways through cranberry bogs and pines.

top_courses.name: Captains Golf Course (Port)
top_courses.must_know: 36 holes. Port Course is the championship layout. Municipal but plays like a private club.

hidden_gems.name: Bayberry Hills Golf Course
hidden_gems.must_know: Municipal course in South Yarmouth. Great shape for a muni. Quiet.

hidden_gems.name: Chatham Seaside Links
hidden_gems.must_know: 9-hole links course right in Chatham village. Walking only. Charming.

lodging_options.name: Wequassett Resort
lodging_options.note: Luxury Cape resort. More couples-oriented but stunning.

lodging_options.name: Cape Cod VRBO cottages
lodging_options.note: Classic Cape cottages. Book early for summer — they fill fast.

lodging_options.name: Chatham Bars Inn / Ocean Edge Resort
lodging_options.note: Classic New England inns. Ocean Edge has its own golf course.

dining.name: The Lobster Pot (Provincetown)
dining.must_know: Iconic Cape Cod lobster. Worth the drive to P-town.

dining.name: Chatham Bars Inn Beach House Grill
dining.must_know: Oceanfront dining. Lobster bake on the beach. Special occasion spot.

dining.name: Arnold's Lobster & Clam Bar
dining.must_know: Eastham institution. Fried clams are the best on the Cape.

non_golf_activities: Beach day at Race Point or Nauset
insider_tips: Highland Links is the experience, not the conditioning. Expect firm, fast, links-style. It's golf as it was 100 years ago.
Book summer tee times and lodging by March — Cape Cod fills up fast.
September is the secret month: warm, less crowded, lower prices, courses in great shape.
Bring a windbreaker even in August — ocean breezes make mornings cool.
The Outer Cape (Wellfleet, Truro, Provincetown) has the best beaches and most character.

activities: Arrive BOS, drive to Cape (90 min)

destinations.avoid_reason: Wisconsin winter. Courses closed. Brutal cold.
